Where AE support fits

When good opportunities are waiting too long for attention.

An AE can step in when follow up is slow, ownership is unclear, or your current team simply has more opportunities than time.

  • Your Head of Sales is carrying too many opportunities
  • Qualified meetings are not receiving consistent follow up
  • A new market or segment needs dedicated coverage
  • Internal AEs need relief without a long recruiting cycle

Discovery

Run structured conversations that clarify the problem, fit, stakeholders, timing, and next step.

Demos and presentations

Support product or service presentations using the client’s approved process and materials.

Follow up

Keep momentum after the meeting with clear ownership, relevant communication, and defined next actions.

Opportunity management

Maintain stage discipline, notes, actions, and visibility inside the agreed sales workflow.

Stakeholder coordination

Map the buying group and help move conversations beyond a single point of contact.

Pipeline review

Review movement, blockers, conversion, and next steps with management and the client team.

Clear ownership

A booked meeting needs someone to own what happens next.

We define the handoff, the follow up, and the next action so qualified interest does not disappear after the calendar invite.

Frequently asked

Outsourced AE questions

We shape the role around your product, process, sales cycle, and team.

What parts of the sales process can an outsourced AE support?

It can cover discovery, demos, follow up, opportunity management, CRM updates, pipeline movement, and close coordination. We agree on the exact scope before the work starts.

Do we need an existing sales process?

A clear offer, target market, and basic sales process help. We can help organize the workflow, but the model works best when you have a real customer problem and some evidence that the market will buy.

Can an AE work with our internal SDRs?

Yes. The AE can work with your internal SDRs or ours as long as everyone agrees on what qualifies, who owns the next step, and how the handoff is recorded.

How is AE performance managed?

We agree on the stages, follow up expectations, opportunity reviews, and reporting, then our manager stays close to the work.
